correctness.rationale: For \(p,q\ge3\), equal-neighborhood twin pairs and three exceptional forts are necessary obstructions. The proof enumerates all eight admissible three-white types and provides an explicit force sequence in each, then extends downwards by monotonicity. No admissible four-white set exists. Exact binomial counting yields the stated four polynomial coefficients. The included direct verifier checks 22,656 initial sets on twelve boards and recomputes minimal forts on four boards. Finite tests are corroborative, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The operation of subdividing one edge is a natural local perturbation of a well-studied dense graph family. The theorem classifies its complete fort obstruction hypergraph and all zero-forcing configurations, showing that the known minimum cardinality is unchanged but the multiplicity of optimal sets increases from pq to 3pq-p-q. The all-coefficient distribution gives a distinct and useful perturbation invariant, beyond a routine recomputation of a scalar parameter.
